item.title: Today at Rodeo Houston: Events, contests, and today's concert performer
item.description: Get the daily schedule for RodeoHouston, including events, contests, and today's concert performer. Don't miss out on the fun!

item.title: Legendary football coach Lou Holtz dies at 89
item.description: The Hall of Famer died in Orlando, his family announced on Wednesday.

item.title: Two men arrested in car chase in southwest Houston, HPD said
item.description: Two people were arrested after a brief car chase on Tuesday in the Greenway Plaza area, police said.

item.title: Talarico beats Crockett in Texas Democratic Senate primary
item.description: Talarico pulled through with a majority of support on Tuesday, avoiding a runoff.

item.title: Texas House Republicans call on Congress to freeze immigration programs
item.description: A group of 55 Republicans in the Texas House of Representatives signed a letter this week calling on Congress to freeze immigration programs in the wake of the deadly shooting at an Austin bar.

item.title: Search continues for suspects in death of Fort Bend County deputy
item.description: Authorities are still looking for clues into the deadly hit-and-run crash that took the life of a Fort Bend County deputy last month.

item.title: Camp Mystic victim's family asks a Texas judge to prevent the facility from reopening
item.description: A Texas judge is hearing evidence on whether Camp Mystic, where 25 girls and two counselors were killed in catastrophic floods last year, should remain closed.

item.title: Trump endorsement will come soon in the Texas Senate runoff between Paxton and Cornyn
item.description: President Trump is warning that the divisive contest “cannot, for the good of the Party, and our Country, itself, be allowed to go on any longer.”

item.title: 2026 Texas Primary Elections: Latest local results
item.description: Voters in Houston and around Texas are heading to the polls on Tuesday in a crucial set of primary elections that will have ramifications at the federal, state and local levels.

item.title: Texas bans candy and sugary drinks from SNAP benefits starting April 1
item.description: Beginning April 1, Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program SNAP recipients in Texas can no longer use their benefits to buy candy or sweetened drinks.
